source: Offshore T&I of the ST-CGF jacket: launch (2021-4589-66-0007), floatation & upending (2021-4589-66-0009), and the Blender scene STT2B_CGF_Jacket_Light.blend

markers.name: Step3 Jacket floating level - tugs pick up slack
Tow jacket via corridor to EN3000 (time-lapse)
Jacket at upending position - tugs hold

notes: Launching barge 142.5 m x 36 m x 8.5 m, mean draft 4.48 m before launch; vessel layout pending confirmation.
Design water depth for the bottom clearance during launch is 52.30 m (LAT); LAT is -2.80 m from MSL.
Results are for a dynamic friction of 0.05 and a winch speed of 0.30 m/s, from the ST-CGF launch analysis report 2021-4589-6K-1015_XA.
Jacket weight and COG are from the MOSES model; the Offshore Installation Contractor decides the final barge trim and draft for launch.

upending.drawing: ST-CGF Jacket Floatation & Upending Installation Sequence, 2021-4589-66-0009-01/-02 Rev 2 (TPGM 220480C-1100-DW-3601-7409)
notes: Elevations are from MSL; dimensions in mm unless stated. Mudline is at EL (-) 52.300 m and the water level at (-) 2.80 m LAT.
The upending sequence is based on a jacket weight of 5435 MT (factored, no sensitivity on COG); results for the weight and COG sensitivity cases are in brackets.
Four slings are used (rows A2, A5, C2 and C5). Internal compartment pressure is assumed to be 0.3 bar.
Controlled flooding is needed for the buoyancy tanks and legs; free flooding may be used for compartments that can be manually flooded and lie below the waterline.
The minimum required seabed clearance during upending is 2.1 m for all cases. The Offshore Installation Contractor develops the final upending sequences.
Results are from the jacket floatation & upending analysis report 2021-4589-6J-1016 Rev 2.

buoyancy_tanks.note: centre tank, not in the model

stages.name: Jacket free floating
actions: Jacket free floating with the lifting slings connected to the padeyes.

stages.name: Flood buoyancy tank BT-H0-C
actions: Commence controlled flooding of buoyancy tank BT-H0-C to 100%.

stages.name: Lift the hook to 42 m
actions: Lift the hook to a height of 42 m from the water surface.

stages.name: Flood buoyancy tanks BT-A2-1 and BT-A5-1 to 30%
actions: Maintain the hook at 42 m from the water surface.
Commence controlled flooding of buoyancy tanks BT-A2-1 and BT-A5-1 to 30%.

stages.name: Lift the hook to 47 m
actions: Lift the hook to a height of 47 m from the water surface.

stages.name: Flood legs L-B5-2 and L-B2-2
actions: Maintain the hook at 47 m from the water surface.
Commence free flooding of legs L-B5-2 and L-B2-2 to 100%.

stages.name: Flood legs L-B5-1, L-B2-1, L-C2-1 and L-C5-1
actions: Maintain the hook at 47 m from the water surface.
Commence free flooding of leg L-B5-1 to 100% and controlled flooding of legs L-B2-1 to 50%, L-C2-1 to 53% and L-C5-1 to 53%.

stages.name: Lower the hook to 43 m, 1 m above the seabed
actions: Lower the main hook to 43 m from the water surface.
The jacket is 1 m from the seabed, for ROV inspection.

stages.name: Lower the hook to 42 m, prepare for on-bottom
actions: Lower the main hook to 42 m from the water surface.

stages.name: On-bottom condition
actions: All jacket leg compartments are flooded up to water level; buoyancy tanks at rows A2, A5, C2, C5 and H0 are 100% flooded.
Open the drain caisson ABH-6204 (J-tube OD 273 x 12.7 WT) and the caissons ABH-4901A and ABH-4901B, flooded up to water level.
See the jacket on-bottom stability analysis and mudmat design report 2021-4589-6J-1017 for the minimum and maximum on-bottom weight.

steps.title: Barge arrives under tow with the jacket
text: The launch barge, carrying the jacket on its skid ways, is towed to the launch location by the lead tug.
Water depth at the launch location is 52.30 m (LAT); the barge mean draft is 4.48 m.

steps.title: Tugs 1 and 2 approach and connect
text: Tug 1 approaches the stern on the starboard side and receives its tow line.
Tug 2 approaches the stern on the port side and receives its tow line.

steps.title: Tugs 3 and 4 connect, all tugs on station
text: Tugs 3 and 4 take position on the port and starboard quarters and receive their lines.
All four tugs are on station and hold the barge for the launch.

steps.title: Ballast the barge to launch trim
text: OIC ballasts the barge to the launch trim and draft (final trim and draft are decided by OIC).
The barge is trimmed by the stern so that the jacket can slide along the skid ways under the winch pull.

steps.title: Launch stage 1: Pre-launch
text: Winch pulls the jacket along the skid ways towards the stern; the jacket weight (5340 MT) rests on the skid ways and the rocker arm.
Launch results are for a dynamic friction of 0.05 and a winch speed of 0.30 m/s.
Drawing time 0 s, jacket velocity 0 m/s.

steps.title: Launch stage 2: Tipping
text: The jacket reaches the rocker arm pins and tips: the rocker arm rotates about its pivot.
Maximum pin reaction: 3383 MT port (3387 MT extreme), 1916 MT starboard (1923 MT extreme).
Drawing time 34.8 s, jacket velocity 2.06 m/s.

steps.title: Launch stage 3: Maximum vessel submergence
text: The jacket slides off the rocker arm and enters the water; the stern of the barge reaches its maximum submergence.
Drawing time 36.7 s, jacket velocity 1.85 m/s.

steps.title: Launch stage 4: Separation
text: The jacket separates from the barge and rotates about its own centre of buoyancy in the water.
Drawing time 42.9 s, jacket velocity 4.5 m/s.

steps.title: Launch stage 5: Jacket minimum bottom clearance
text: The jacket is at its minimum clearance from the seabed, 5.40 m (water depth 52.30 m LAT).
Maximum pin reaction during the launch: 3387 MT.
Drawing time 46 s, jacket velocity 2.48 m/s.

steps.title: Launch stage 6: Final position
text: The jacket settles to its floating position. Jacket buoyancy 7317 MT against a weight of 5340 MT: minimum reserve buoyancy 27%.
Drawing time 150 s.

steps.title: Jacket floats level, tugs pick up the slack
text: The jacket floats level and the tugs take up their lines on the jacket; the barge is released.

steps.title: Barge towed away
text: The launch barge, under tow by the lead tug, is towed clear of the jacket.

steps.title: Crane vessel moves in alongside the jacket
text: The jacket stays where it was launched, held by the four tugs. The tugs on the crane side open up to give way.
The crane vessel SK3500 comes in with the launch barge gone, and takes position parallel to the jacket, clear of it, with its crane stowed along the hull.

steps.title: Crane reaches out over the jacket, slings connected
text: The crane slews its boom over the side until the hook is above the lifting padeyes; the vessel stays clear of the jacket.
The main hook is lowered and the four lifting slings (rows A2, A5, C2 and C5) are connected to the upending padeyes; the jacket floats freely with the slings connected.

steps.title: Upending stage 1: Flood buoyancy tank BT-H0-C
text: Commence controlled flooding of buoyancy tank BT-H0-C to 100%.

steps.title: Upending stage 2: Lift the hook to 42 m
text: Lift the hook to a height of 42 m from the water surface.

steps.title: Upending stage 3: Flood buoyancy tanks BT-A2-1 and BT-A5-1 to 30%
text: Maintain the hook at 42 m from the water surface.
Commence controlled flooding of buoyancy tanks BT-A2-1 and BT-A5-1 to 30%.

steps.title: Upending stage 4: Lift the hook to 47 m
text: Lift the hook to a height of 47 m from the water surface.

steps.title: Upending stage 5: Flood legs L-B5-2 and L-B2-2
text: Maintain the hook at 47 m from the water surface.
Commence free flooding of legs L-B5-2 and L-B2-2 to 100%.

steps.title: Upending stage 6: Flood legs L-B5-1, L-B2-1, L-C2-1 and L-C5-1
text: Maintain the hook at 47 m from the water surface.
Commence free flooding of leg L-B5-1 to 100% and controlled flooding of legs L-B2-1 to 50%, L-C2-1 to 53% and L-C5-1 to 53%.

steps.title: Upending stage 7: Lower the hook to 43 m, 1 m above the seabed
text: Lower the main hook to 43 m from the water surface.
The jacket is 1 m from the seabed, for ROV inspection.

steps.title: Upending stage 8: Lower the hook to 42 m, prepare for on-bottom
text: Lower the main hook to 42 m from the water surface.
Prepare for the on-bottom condition.

steps.title: Upending stage 9: On-bottom condition
text: Jacket at the seabed.
All jacket leg compartments are flooded up to water level; buoyancy tanks at rows A2, A5, C2, C5 and H0 are 100% flooded.
Open the drain caisson ABH-6204 (J-tube OD 273 x 12.7 WT) and the caissons ABH-4901A and ABH-4901B, flooded up to water level.
See the jacket on-bottom stability analysis and mudmat design report 2021-4589-6J-1017 for the minimum and maximum on-bottom weight.
